zh.q: 赤道为什么是一条低压带？
zh.concl: 赤道接受的太阳辐射多，近地面空气受热膨胀上升、气压降低，形成赤道低压带（热力成因）。
points: 赤道地区接受太阳辐射能量多，近地面空气受热膨胀上升，空气密度减小，气压降低。
教材假设地球表面是均匀的：引起大气运动的只有高、低纬度的受热不均和地转偏向力。
赤道低压带是热力成因：由冷热差异直接造成。

zh.q: 升上去的空气，为什么走到 30° 就下沉？
zh.concl: 地转偏向力让高空气流在 30° 附近偏成西风，空气堆积下沉，形成副热带高压带；东北信风与东南信风在赤道辐合上升，组成低纬环流。
points: 赤道上升的暖空气在高空向南北分流；向北的一支逐渐右偏成西南风，到北纬 30° 附近高空偏成西风。
空气在这里不断堆积下沉，使地面气压升高，形成副热带高压带（动力成因）。
下沉后近地面分两支：向南右偏成东北信风，向北右偏成西南风（盛行西风）；东北信风与东南信风在赤道辐合上升。

zh.q: 60° 附近为什么又出现一条低压带？
zh.concl: 暖空气沿极锋爬升，形成副极地低压带（动力成因）；北半球由此有三个环流圈，南半球同样有三个。
points: 北极终年寒冷，空气堆积下沉，形成极地高压带；向南流的气流右偏成东北风，叫极地东风。
极地东风在北纬 60° 附近与较暖的盛行西风相遇，暖空气爬升，在两条高压带之间形成相对的低压带——副极地低压带（动力成因）。
低纬环流、高纬环流由冷热差异直接驱动；中纬环流夹在中间被带动，方向与两侧相反。

zh.q: 七个气压带、六个风带，是一条线还是绕地球一圈？
zh.concl: 带是绕地球一圈的环。全球 7 个气压带、6 个风带；风向由高压指向低压，再按北半球右偏、南半球左偏。
points: 气压带、风带都是绕地球一圈的环带，不是一条线；风带是一个纬度范围里的盛行风。
北半球：低纬信风带吹东北风，中纬西风带吹西南风（盛行西风），极地东风带吹东北风。
南半球镜像：东南信风、西北风（盛行西风）、东南风（极地东风）。

zh.q: 直射点北移以后，罗马的夏天为什么变干？
zh.concl: 气压带、风带随直射点移动，北半球夏季偏北、冬季偏南；罗马夏季受副热带高压带控制、冬季受西风带控制，形成夏干冬雨的地中海气候。
points: 由于太阳直射点的南北移动，气压带和风带在一年内做周期性的季节移动。
在北半球，与二分日相比，气压带和风带的位置大致是夏季偏北、冬季偏南。
纬度 30°—40° 的大陆西部，夏季受副热带高压带控制、炎热干燥，冬季受西风带控制、温和多雨，形成地中海气候。

zh.q: 1 月的亚洲，为什么出现一个巨大的高压？
zh.concl: 海陆热力差异使北半球纬向的气压带被分裂成高、低气压中心：1 月亚洲高压切断副极地低压带，7 月亚洲低压切断副热带高压带；气压中心随季节变化，形成季风。
points: 冬季陆地降温比海洋快，出现冷高压；夏季陆地增温比海洋快，出现热低压。
北半球陆地面积大、海陆相间，纬向的气压带被分裂为一个个高、低气压中心；南半球 30°S 以南基本呈带状。
气压中心的季节变化使盛行风向随季节变换，形成季风：东亚冬季吹西北季风，夏季吹东南季风。

zh.q: 考核：麦哲伦船队的四段航程，各受哪个带控制？
zh.concl: 盛行西风 → 逆风；副热带高压带 → 平静无风；东南信风 → 顺风；赤道低压带 → 风平浪静。
points: 南美洲南端的海峡受盛行西风影响，船队向西逆风航行。
30°S 附近受副热带高压带控制，气流下沉，平静无风，天气炎热，航行十分艰难。
进入东南信风带后顺风航行，最为轻松；到赤道附近，受赤道低压带控制，风平浪静。

en.q: Why is the equator a belt of low pressure?
en.concl: The equator receives more solar radiation; near-surface air is heated, expands and rises and the pressure drops, forming the equatorial low-pressure belt (thermal origin).
points: The equatorial region receives more solar radiation; near-surface air is heated, expands and rises, its density falls and the pressure drops.
The textbook assumes a uniform Earth surface: the only causes of atmospheric motion are uneven heating between high and low latitudes and the Coriolis force.
The equatorial low has a thermal origin: it is caused directly by the temperature difference.

en.q: Why does air that has risen sink when it reaches 30°?
en.concl: The Coriolis force turns upper-level flow into a westerly near 30°, where air piles up and sinks to form the subtropical high; the northeast and southeast trades converge and rise at the equator, forming the Hadley cell.
points: Warm air rising at the equator splits north and south aloft; the northward branch gradually veers right into a southwest wind and becomes a westerly aloft near 30°N.
Air keeps piling up and sinking here, raising the surface pressure and forming the subtropical high-pressure belt (dynamic origin).

After sinking it splits into two branches near the surface: southward it veers right into the northeast trades, northward it veers right into southwest winds (the prevailing westerlies); the northeast and southeast trades converge and rise at the equator.

en.q: Why is there another belt of low pressure near 60°?
en.concl: Warm air climbs along the polar front to form the subpolar low (dynamic origin); so the Northern Hemisphere has three circulation cells, and so does the Southern.
points: The Arctic is cold all year, so air piles up and sinks, forming the polar high; flow heading south veers right into a northeast wind, the polar easterlies.

Near 60°N the polar easterlies meet the warmer prevailing westerlies and the warm air climbs, forming a relatively low-pressure belt between the two high-pressure belts: the subpolar low (dynamic origin).
The Hadley and polar cells are driven directly by temperature differences; the Ferrel cell between them is dragged along and turns the opposite way.

en.q: Seven pressure belts and six wind belts: are they lines, or do they circle the globe?
en.concl: The belts are rings around the globe: 7 pressure belts and 6 wind belts worldwide; wind blows from high to low pressure, then deflects right in the north and left in the south.
points: Pressure and wind belts are bands circling the globe, not lines; a wind belt is the prevailing wind over a range of latitudes.
Northern Hemisphere: the trade wind belt blows northeast winds, the westerly belt southwest winds (prevailing westerlies), the polar easterly belt northeast winds.
Southern Hemisphere mirror: southeast trades, northwest winds (prevailing westerlies), southeast winds (polar easterlies).

en.q: After the subsolar point moves north, why does Rome's summer become dry?
en.concl: Pressure and wind belts follow the subsolar point, lying farther north in the Northern Hemisphere summer and farther south in winter; Rome is under the subtropical high in summer and the westerlies in winter, giving a Mediterranean climate with dry summers and wet winters.
points: Because the subsolar point moves north and south, the pressure and wind belts shift seasonally over the year.
In the Northern Hemisphere, compared with the equinoxes, the pressure and wind belts lie roughly farther north in summer and farther south in winter.
On the western side of continents at 30°–40° latitude, summer is controlled by the subtropical high (hot and dry) and winter by the westerlies (mild and rainy), giving a Mediterranean climate.

en.q: Why does a huge high-pressure system appear over Asia in January?
en.concl: Land–sea thermal contrast breaks the Northern Hemisphere's zonal pressure belts into high and low centers: in January the Asian high cuts the subpolar low, in July the Asian low cuts the subtropical high; the centers change with the seasons, forming monsoons.
points: In winter land cools faster than the ocean, producing a cold high; in summer land warms faster than the ocean, producing a thermal low.

The Northern Hemisphere has large land areas alternating with ocean, so the zonal pressure belts break up into separate high and low pressure centers; south of 30°S the Southern Hemisphere stays largely banded.
Seasonal changes in the pressure centers make prevailing winds change with the seasons, forming monsoons: East Asia has northwest monsoons in winter and southeast monsoons in summer.

en.q: Assessment: which belt controlled each of the four legs of Magellan's voyage?
en.concl: Prevailing westerlies → headwind; subtropical high → calm; southeast trades → tailwind; equatorial low → calm seas.
points: The strait at the southern tip of South America is under the prevailing westerlies, so the fleet sailing west faced headwinds.
Near 30°S the subtropical high controls; air sinks, it's calm and hot, and sailing was very hard.
Once in the southeast trade wind belt the fleet sailed with the wind, the easiest leg; near the equator, under the equatorial low, the seas were calm.
